title: How I keep AI coding agents from approving their own work: two outside reviewers on every plan and diff
author: Massive-State2698
selftext:
I'm a software architect with 20+ years of experience, and Melbees, a word puzzle on a honeycomb, is a game I build. AI coding agents write the code, so most of the work is in how the work is organized. This post is that part, in the order a task goes through it.

Every task starts as an issue. Nothing is built from a chat message or from anyone's memory: the issue is the record, and the plan that answers it is a file in the repository with the original request quoted at the top. If the plan touches the architecture, it can't ship without a line quoting the architect's approval, so the design only changes on purpose.

For a task in the full mission loop, two reviewers check the plan and then the diff. The conducting agent never reviews its own work, the fixed reviewer always comes from a different vendor than the conductor, and an unavailable reviewer is replaced under written rules. Before judging the plan, each reviewer is asked what it would do differently, so the round starts with a second design instead of a rubber stamp. A plan moves on only when both reviewers have no open blocker, and a blocker is cleared by argument, never outvoted.

After the diff review comes a local gate: one command that runs the checks and the tests selected for the files that changed and blocks what fails. The last step is a script that lands the change on the main branch and refuses a plan that doesn't say how it lands.

Why reviewers outside the session? The failure I care about is a model agreeing with itself. The process treats whatever the agents deliver as something to specify, review and validate, never to trust because it sounds sure.

The architect directing the project also develops AI solutions professionally.

AI note: the code is written by AI coding agents (Claude Code and Codex); the architecture, the specs and the final call are mine, and AI helped me draft this post.

If you're curious about the game, today's Daily Challenge runs free in the browser: https://daily.melbees.games/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=novembro&utm_content=p-logica-aigamedev

How do you separate implementation from review in your AI workflow, and what do you require before accepting a reviewer's verdict?
